name: Millencolin
label: Epitaph
lede: Named after a skate trick, built in Örebro, and still the same four guys thirty years later.

eras.title: Skate rats from Örebro
eras.text: Three friends bonded over skateboarding and Bad Religion start a band in a Swedish city most of the world can't place. By 1994 they have a drummer, two demos and a deal with Burning Heart.

years.h: Three friends in Örebro start a band named after a skate trick
years.p: [[Nikola Šarčević|6afaaf35-5be3-4212-8a83-614acff5571b]], Mathias Färm and Erik Ohlsson form Millencolin on October 12, 1992. The name is a spelling twist on the skateboard trick 'melancholy'.

years.h: Fredrik Larzon takes over the drums
years.p: Färm had started on drums; when Fredrik Larzon arrives, Färm moves to rhythm guitar and the four-piece that still exists today is set.

years.h: Two demos, Goofy and Melack
years.p: The band records the Goofy demo in early 1993 and Melack in the summer, then follows with the Use Your Nose single in November on Burning Heart.

years.h: The Skauch EP and Tiny Tunes arrive on Burning Heart
years.p: Skauch comes out in July 1994 and the debut album Tiny Tunes follows the same year, both on Sweden's Burning Heart Records.

eras.title: Life on a Plate, Epitaph and the Warped bus
eras.text: An album cover drawn by their own guitarist and a Brett Gurewitz-run label carry Millencolin out of Sweden. By the end of the decade they are touring on three continents.

years.h: Life on a Plate hits Sweden, with a cover by Erik Ohlsson
years.p: Recorded in August 1995 at Unisound in Örebro, it is released on October 11 by Burning Heart. Slitz magazine names Ohlsson's cover art Sweden's Album Cover of the Year.
years.xp:
The album reaches number 4 in Sweden and is later certified gold there, per Wikipedia. Its single 'The Story of My Life' came out in September 1995.

It is the record that gets Epitaph Records interested, and the label releases it in North America in 1996.

years.h: Epitaph puts out Life on a Plate in North America
years.p: Brett Gurewitz's label releases the album on March 26, 1996, and 'Move Your Car' is issued as a single that October.

years.h: For Monkeys, cut in a month with a death-metal engineer
years.p: Recorded in January 1997 at Unisound with engineer Dan Swanö, best known for death and black metal, it brings 'Lozin' Must' and its video. Epitaph follows in May.
years.xp: Mathias Färm co-writes three songs on the record: 'Trendy Winds', 'Light's Out' and 'Lowlife'. 'Twenty Two' is a second single.

years.h: On the 1997 Warped Tour
years.p: Millencolin joins the Warped Tour, the American summer circuit that put them in front of skate punk crowds far from Örebro.

years.h: A Warner Bros. dispute turns Tiny Tunes into Same Old Tunes
years.p: Legal trouble with Warner Brothers forces the band to re-release their debut in 1998 under a new title, Same Old Tunes.

eras.title: Brett Gurewitz, Hollywood and a video game
eras.text: The band leaves Sweden to record for the first time, drops most of the ska and lands a song on the game every skater is playing.

years.h: Pennybridge Pioneers, recorded at Westbeach with Brett Gurewitz
years.p: Made July to September 1999 in Hollywood with the Epitaph Records boss producing, it is Millencolin's first album cut outside Sweden and comes out February 22, 2000.
years.xp:
The record moves away from the band's ska-punk roots toward a more alternative rock sound. The title is a joke: Örebro translates roughly as 'Pennybridge'.

Singles are 'Penguins & Polarbears', 'Fox' and 'No Cigar'. It reached number 13 in Australia and went platinum there by May 2001, per Wikipedia.

years.h: 'No Cigar' lands in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2
years.p: The single 'No Cigar' is on the game's soundtrack, and returns in later Tony Hawk remakes, putting a band from Örebro in front of a generation of skaters.

years.h: Home from Home with producer Lou Giordano
years.p: Recorded September 15 to October 17, 2001 at Little Big Room in Haninge, it is out March 12, 2002 and reaches number 3 in Australia.
years.xp: Singles are 'Kemp', 'Man or Mouse' and 'Battery Check', each with a video. On the tour that followed, drummer Fredrik Larzon injured his elbow and needed surgery, so stand-ins covered while he recovered, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Hometown heroes
eras.text: Awards at home, a Swedish number 2 album and a skatepark of their own. Millencolin becomes an Örebro institution.

years.h: Best Swedish Rock at the Swedish Hit Awards
years.p: The band wins the category in 2003, a mainstream nod for a skate punk band who started out in a rehearsal room in Örebro.

years.h: Kingwood reaches number 2 in Sweden
years.p: Produced by Chips Kiesbye and out March 30, 2005 in Sweden, it is Millencolin's highest Swedish chart placing, per Wikipedia. 'Farewell My Hell' began as a Nikola Šarčević solo idea.
years.xp: It was recorded August to October 2004 in Örebro and Gothenburg. 'Farewell My Hell' later appears prominently in the Swedish vampire comedy Frostbite. The band toured Europe with Street Dogs and The Lawrence Arms and played the 2005 Warped Tour.

years.h: The Millencolin Open at their own skatepark
years.p: The band runs an annual skateboard contest at a skatepark they own in Örebro, tying the music back to the trick behind their name.

years.h: Machine 15, the last record for seven years
years.p: The 2008 album is followed by a seven-year gap in studio releases.

eras.title: Twenty years, a hometown party
eras.text: A football song, a two-day birthday festival and a comeback album keep the four original members busy after the long quiet.

years.h: 'Örebro' debuts at Eyravallen stadium
years.p: The band writes a single for local football club Örebro SK and plays it for the first time at the club's Eyravallen stadium.

years.h: Millencolin throws its own 20 Year Festival in Örebro
years.p: Two days in June 2012 of exclusive sets and international guests to mark two decades since October 1992.

years.h: True Brew brings them back after seven years
years.p: The album, released in April 2015, takes on European nationalism and racism. They play Slam Dunk Festival that May.

years.h: SOS, recorded in their own Soundlab studio
years.p: Their ninth album comes out on Epitaph on February 15, 2019, recorded at Soundlab in Örebro and mixed by Jens Bogren. It reaches number 15 in Sweden.

sources.title: Louder: A Short History Of Millencolin
